title: OpenAI Just Killed Its Side Quests and Merged Everything Into One App. The Indian AI Workforce Should Be Watching Closely.
excerpt: Greg Brockman consolidates ChatGPT, Codex, and the developer API into a single 'agentic super app' — a restructuring that reshapes the platform thousands of Indian engineers build on, and compete against.
body:
In the clearest signal yet that the age of sprawling AI product portfolios is over, OpenAI has merged its three major products — ChatGPT, Codex, and its developer API — into a single unified platform under co-founder and president Greg Brockman. The restructuring, announced internally on May 16, formalises an interim arrangement that began when Fidji Simo, OpenAI's CEO of AGI deployment, went on medical leave in early April.

## One Platform, One Boss

Brockman's internal memo left little room for ambiguity. "We're consolidating our product efforts to execute with maximum focus toward the agentic future, to win across both consumer and enterprise," he wrote. The new structure places four pillars under his leadership: Thibault Sottiaux, the engineer behind Codex's rapid growth, now leads core product and platform across consumer, enterprise, and developer surfaces. Nick Turley, who steered ChatGPT's expansion to more than 900 million weekly active users, moves to an enterprise-focused role. Brockman himself retains oversight of AI infrastructure, including the Stargate data centre programme.

The consolidation is the culmination of a strategic retreat that began in December, when CEO Sam Altman declared a "code red" and demanded the company refocus on its core ChatGPT experience. Since then, OpenAI has shut down Sora, its video generation app — which consumed enormous computing resources relative to its revenue and torpedoed a planned billion-dollar Disney investment. It shelved its adult mode for ChatGPT. It halted OpenAI for Science. Internally, the company has taken to calling these abandoned initiatives "side quests."

## The Compute Crunch

The rationale is partly mathematical. Brockman explained on a recent podcast that OpenAI's computing power is "not enough for even a personal assistant and the Codex line." When compute is the binding constraint, maintaining separate product teams, separate roadmaps, and separate engineering organisations for converging capabilities is an unaffordable luxury. The merger eliminates that redundancy and concentrates resources on a single surface capable of conversation, code generation, autonomous task execution, web browsing, and file management — all powered by the same underlying model.

The competitive pressure is immediate and intense. Cursor, the AI coding tool, has reached $2 billion in annualised revenue and is reportedly raising at a $50 billion valuation. Anthropic's Claude Code has gained traction with enterprise developers. Google's Gemini has grown its share of AI web traffic from 5.7 per cent to 21.5 per cent over the past twelve months, according to SimilarWeb, while ChatGPT's share has declined from 86.7 per cent to 64.5 per cent.

## Why the Indian Tech Ecosystem Should Care

The restructuring carries outsized implications for India's technology sector. Indian engineers form one of the largest contingents in Silicon Valley's AI workforce, and OpenAI's platform is the foundation upon which thousands of Indian startups — from Bangalore's AI-first SaaS companies to Hyderabad's enterprise automation shops — have built their products.

A unified platform means a single API surface, which should simplify integration. But it also means OpenAI will increasingly compete directly with the tools that Indian developers have been building on top of its infrastructure. When the platform itself becomes an autonomous coding agent, a productivity suite, and an enterprise workflow engine, the value of the middleware layer — where many Indian startups operate — compresses sharply.

For Indian engineers at rival companies, the landscape is shifting too. Sundar Pichai's Google, where Indian-origin engineers hold key leadership positions across Gemini and DeepMind, is OpenAI's most formidable competitor. Satya Nadella's Microsoft, OpenAI's largest investor, must now reconcile its own Copilot strategy with a partner that is building a competing unified platform.

## The IPO Calculus

The restructuring is also IPO preparation. OpenAI is targeting a public listing in Q4 2026 at a valuation of approximately $852 billion. A simpler product story — one platform rather than a portfolio of separate apps — is easier to pitch to institutional investors. It creates a cleaner revenue narrative: one subscription tier, one developer platform, one enterprise offering, all building on the same model infrastructure.

Whether one person can run both product strategy and infrastructure for a company with 900 million weekly users, a multi-billion-dollar data centre programme, and an IPO on the horizon is a question OpenAI's board has implicitly answered by giving Brockman both jobs. The side quests are over. What remains is the main quest: build the platform, ship the agent, go public.
